---
title: "How an analysis moves through fmrimod"
description: "A mental model for the objects and transformations from authored intent to group inference."
---

This page explains what each stage owns, what changes at its boundary, and what
must survive the transition. Read the [golden-path tutorial](../tutorials/golden-path.qmd)
first if you want a runnable analysis. Return here when you need to understand
why the objects are separate.

## The short version

An fmrimod analysis moves from authored meaning to increasingly numerical
representations:

`Spec and terms → realized design → fit → contrast result → group data → group inference`

Each arrow lowers an intention into numbers. The library keeps enough context
alongside those numbers to explain where they came from.

## 1. Author the model as terms

A `Spec` is an immutable, ordered collection of typed terms. Event terms record
conditions, HRF choices, and modulators; baseline terms record intercepts,
trends, and other nuisance structure. Composition with `+` builds a model
description without constructing a matrix.

At this stage, the object preserves research intent and ordering. It does not
yet know the event rows, scan times, or number of design columns. Those enter
when the specification is compiled. See [Design matrices](../tutorials/design-matrices.qmd)
for the authoring workflow and the [`Spec` implementation](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/fmrimod/spec/terms.py)
for the exact data model.

## 2. Realize the design against events and time

Compilation joins the authored terms to an event table and a `SamplingFrame`.
The result is a numerical design together with `DesignColumns`: the map from
matrix columns back to terms, conditions, levels, basis components, and roles.
This provenance is what later lets a semantic contrast ask for an effect by
meaning instead of guessing from a column name.

`SamplingFrame` owns run lengths, one TR per run, run start times, and the
convolution precision. The design owns sampled regressors. These are related,
but neither replaces the other.

An externally constructed matrix can enter through `RealizedDesign`. That is
an interoperability route. Its provenance may be inferred or incomplete, so
semantic resolution can refuse an ambiguous request rather than manufacture a
meaning the matrix does not establish. The distinction is defined in
[`RealizedDesign`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/fmrimod/design/realized.py)
and [`DesignColumns`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/fmrimod/design/columns.py).

## 3. Let the dataset own observations and space

`FmriDataset` binds the observations to their acquisition context: events,
sampling, censoring, and the data adapter. An image-backed adapter can also
carry a mask and affine. A plain feature matrix is valid input, but it does not
imply a three-dimensional geometry.

This boundary preserves which samples and features the numbers represent. It
does not silently add spatial meaning. That is why a matrix-derived result can
be statistically valid while `to_nifti()` remains unavailable. See
[Troubleshooting](../help/troubleshooting.qmd#the-contrast-is-valid-but-spatial-export-fails)
for the repair choices.

## 4. Fit with an explicit solver

`fmri_lm()` combines a specification or realized design with a dataset, then
applies the selected fitting engine. The fit stores coefficients, residual
variance and degrees of freedom, the realized design, column provenance, and
operational provenance such as the solver path and AR or mask status.

The observations have now become parameter estimates and diagnostics. The
design meaning, sample accounting, and spatial context should remain
inspectable on the fit. Rank deficiency is not hidden: the solver can produce
a pseudoinverse solution while reporting which coefficient directions are not
unique. The [rank-diagnostics tests](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/tests/test_glm/test_rank_diagnostics.py)
state that contract.

## 5. Resolve a hypothesis into a `ContrastResult`

A semantic contrast begins as intent: for example, a condition, a difference
between levels, or a joint test over basis components. Resolution uses
`DesignColumns` to turn that intent into weights for the realized design.
Missing or ambiguous provenance is an error with a repair path; fmrimod does
not fall back to a regular-expression guess.

Evaluation produces a `ContrastResult` containing the estimate, statistic,
standard error, p-value, degrees of freedom, statistic type, spatial context,
the contrast intent, and the columns touched. The numerical result changes;
the hypothesis and its provenance remain attached. The
[Contrasts tutorial](../tutorials/contrasts.qmd) shows the supported semantic
forms.

## 6. Move subject results into group analysis

There are two related group containers, chosen by where the subject effects
come from:

- `group_dataset_from_contrasts()` collects named subject `ContrastResult`
  objects into a native `GroupDataset`. It requires compatible contrast names,
  dimensions, and spatial context. It preserves JSON-ready intent and touched-
  column metadata, not Python object identity. `ols_voxelwise()` then fits the
  group model.
- `GroupData` describes validated group inputs stored as CSV, HDF5, NIfTI, or
  first-level results. It is the input container used by `fmri_meta()`,
  `fmri_ttest()`, and `group_fit()`.

In both routes, subject effects become a subject-by-feature group input, then
group estimates and inference. Subject and feature identity, contrast meaning,
and method metadata should survive. First-level residuals and solver internals
do not become group observations.

::: {.callout-important title="Typed containers do not make every group choice typed"}
The first-level specification, design provenance, and contrast intent have
typed representations. Group requests and results also use validated
containers, but group formulas, method names, robustness modes, and backend
selectors are still constrained strings in parts of the public API. Treat
their documented combinations as contracts; do not infer that every
second-level decision is a closed typed algebra.
:::

## What changes, and what should remain

| Transition | New representation | Information that should remain inspectable |
|---|---|---|
| Terms to realized design | Sampled numeric columns | Term, condition, level, basis, role, and column order |
| Dataset plus design to fit | Coefficients, variance, degrees of freedom, diagnostics | Sampling, realized design, column provenance, spatial and fit provenance |
| Contrast intent to result | Weights, estimate, statistic, uncertainty | Intent, touched columns, design/provenance identity, spatial context |
| Subject results to group input | Subject-by-feature arrays or validated file-backed data | Subject and feature names, compatible contrast metadata, geometry when present |
| Group input to inference | Group coefficients, statistics, uncertainty | Formula or design, method/backend choice, subject accounting, result geometry |
